deviations.item: one script and one JSON for the four P1/P3 candidates
deviations.what_you_did: analysis/probes/phase_e_a1_p1_p3.py -> analysis/out/phase_e/a1_p1_p3.json, one block per candidate
deviations.why: the orchestrating task names the item key a1_p1_p3; the per-candidate content is unchanged

deviations.item: artifact checks and strata recompute the separability statistic, not the change-point floor
deviations.prereg_said: AC2/AC3/AC5/AC4/strata: recompute the statistic and apply the candidate's rule; the Probe 1 rule includes the floor-step and floor-transfer downgrades
deviations.what_you_did: each check recomputes fp_share and AUC on its population and applies the Probe 1 verdict rule (probe_1.unit_verdict) with the A1 recheck, FLAT, floor-step and floor-transfer components carried from the B u E computation; floor stability itself is tested by K2 on B u E and on E
deviations.why: the change-point permutation test per subset (up to ~60 subsets) is the expensive part and the checks target the separability statistic; K2 is the pre-registered floor test
deviations.effect_on_verdict: none on the direction of any check: a carried UNSTABLE floor can only hold a check label at or below WEAK, identically for the reference and the check

deviations.item: K2 applied as the Phase B floor rule, never twice
deviations.prereg_said: K2: Phase B change-point rule on B u E and on E; UNSTABLE -> one-level downgrade (Phase B rule)
deviations.what_you_did: the E verdict is the unchanged Probe 1 rule on E, which already turns ALIVE into WEAK when E's floor is UNSTABLE. K2 adds a downgrade only when B u E or E is UNSTABLE (>= 30 series from >= 5 s), the verdict being judged is ALIVE and that downgrade has not already been applied
deviations.why: '(Phase B rule)' is the ALIVE -> WEAK floor rule; applying it again to a label it already lowered would count the same evidence twice
deviations.effect_on_verdict: see kill_tests.K2_floor_stability.result per candidate; under a literal double application a candidate whose E verdict was already floor-downgraded would drop one more level

deviations.item: order of 'take the lower label' checks and one-level downgrades
deviations.prereg_said: AC2, AC3, AC5, P1-K3: FAIL -> take the lower label; AC4, confinement, kill tests: one-level downgrade or cap; order not stated
deviations.what_you_did: min-type checks first (relative to the E label), then downgrades and caps, passed to survival_status() in that order; survival.final_label_other_order gives the label with the downgrades first
deviations.why: this order gives the lower (conservative) label when both kinds fire
deviations.effect_on_verdict: none unless a min-type check FAILs (see survival.checks_in_order)

deviations.prereg_said: join_clean_mask: the call_id does not occur in another session (re-stamped resume/fork copies)
deviations.what_you_did: the 'another session' set is the pooled B u E sessions of the unit (B only for cc_local); synthetic call ids (loader-made 'synthetic:<format>:<seq>', unique only within a session) are excluded from the copy test
deviations.why: H may not be read and A is not allowed here; a synthetic id is not a call id and would mark every OpenCode pair with a redacted id as a copy
deviations.effect_on_verdict: copies shared with A or H sessions are not detected (limitation)

deviations.prereg_said: dominated if one cluster holds > 0.25 of the statistic's denominator events (or contributing sessions), or one session > 0.10
deviations.what_you_did: tested on the eligible W pairs (fp_share denominator) and separately on the eligible G pairs (AUC control); a kind is dominated if either is; each leave-out removes the cluster's sessions from both W and G. A leave-out with W or G below the Probe 1 min n is UNTESTABLE_WITHOUT_DOMINANT
deviations.why: the Probe 1 statistic has two populations; testing both can only add checks

deviations.item: missing repo_id / user_id in AC4 and the strata
deviations.what_you_did: sessions whose repo_id / user_id is null form one cluster labelled 'unknown' (E.dominance already grouped them together); it is ranked, tested and left out like any other cluster
deviations.why: 651 of the 2,000 B sessions have a null user_id; leaving them unassigned would hide a dominant pseudo-cluster
deviations.effect_on_verdict: see artifact_checks.AC4_dominance.leave_outs (the 'unknown' user cluster is a pseudo-cluster, not one person)

deviations.prereg_said: post-stratified ratio estimator sum(w num)/sum(w den) with the session bootstrap
deviations.what_you_did: fp_share: weighted_cluster_rate as written; AUC: pair weights = product of session weights, the same session draws as probe_1.auc_ci (multiplicities); the unweighted control of the same function is reported next to it
deviations.why: the prereg states the estimator for rates only; this is the AUC analogue

deviations.item: AC1 lookup for OpenCode pairs with redacted call ids
deviations.prereg_said: each event is looked up in the raw source by (session_id, uuid or call_id)
deviations.what_you_did: pairs whose raw callID was redacted ('REDACTED', IR id synthetic:opencode:<seq>) are located by their ordinal among the session's tool parts (the loader emits one call per tool part in order); located_by counts both kinds
deviations.why: the release redacted those ids; no other key exists
deviations.effect_on_verdict: none if every audited pair is found (see AC1_parser.found)

deviations.prereg_said: recompute AUC ... after dropping the single session with most G pairs
deviations.what_you_did: step 1 restricts G to subagent/webfetch/websearch; step 2 additionally removes the session with the most eligible restricted-G pairs from both W and G; AUC DEAD at either step -> kill, G below 30 pairs from 5 s at either step -> cap WEAK
deviations.why: 'Then drop the session' (PREREG_E.md 1.3) reads as sequential; a session is dropped whole

deviations.prereg_said: FAIL if >= 2 of 30 differ; survival: SURVIVES needs every artifact check to pass
deviations.what_you_did: an AC1 FAIL is a one-level downgrade
deviations.why: the prereg names no other effect for AC1

deviations.what_you_did: W restricted to one tool_key per stratum, G (the generation-bound control, other tools by construction) kept whole
deviations.why: G has no tool_key in common with W
deviations.effect_on_verdict: none unless CONFINED on the tool axis

deviations.item: P3 stratification, tool and length axes
deviations.prereg_said: stratify by tool, model, repo, length tercile
deviations.what_you_did: model and repo axes computed; tool axis NOT_APPLICABLE (session-level statistic); length axis UNTESTABLE (all long sessions sit in the top A tercile by construction)

deviations.prereg_said: K1-K3 thresholds; every second-pass statistic runs on B u E
deviations.what_you_did: K1-K3 decided on B u E; K1/K2 on E reported alongside
deviations.effect_on_verdict: none unless the E value would cross a threshold that B u E does not (see kill_tests)

deviations.prereg_said: probe3 verdict: Wilson hi <= 0.20 for ALIVE
deviations.what_you_did: the weighted share uses the session-bootstrap hi of weighted_cluster_rate in place of the Wilson hi
deviations.why: a Wilson interval has no weighted form here
deviations.effect_on_verdict: none unless the weighted hi crosses 0.20

verdict_cells_computed.multiplicity: verdicts are descriptive per mechanism x unit x split; no family-wise correction. Every output JSON reports the number of verdict cells it computed.
